## SFX architecture question

You asked whether cards should play SFX through the normal Feel Sound Manager mixer path, or via per-VFX `MMF_Player`/playlist setups, and whether I can wire up an `MMF_Player` per card myself.

Quick recommendation: **keep the current approach, don't switch to per-card MMF_Players.** Here's why, and what I found:

- The codebase already has a clean, centralized system: `CardSfxCue` + `CardSfxPlayer.Play(cue, position)`, which routes every card SFX through `MMSoundManager`'s Sfx track (respecting the mixer volume sliders in Options, playlists for variation, etc.). Every VFX controller already just calls `CardSfxPlayer.Play(_someSfxCue, position)` at the right beat in its own sequence (impact, contact, etc.) — that's precisely why sequencing (e.g. "SFX plays after the negation panel closes," "impact SFX plays exactly when the projectile lands") already works correctly throughout this session's earlier fixes.
- Switching to a dedicated `MMF_Player` per card would mean: building a Feel feedback asset for every single card (~20+), each just to do what `CardSfxPlayer.Play` already does in one line, but now needing its own playlist/volume/randomization config kept in sync with the shared mixer settings by hand. It's substantially more setup surface for no behavioral gain — the current cue-based system already gets you mixer routing, playlists, and position-based 2D/3D handling.
- `MMF_Player` is the right tool when you want a **single reusable, designer-tunable bundle of several simultaneous feedbacks** (sound + shake + flash + haptics) triggered from one place with no code — which is exactly what `_feedbackLightHit`/`_feedbackMediumHit`/`_feedbackHeavyHit` already are, for the *generic* hit-impact feel shared across all cards. That's the correct use of MMF_Player here, and it's already in place.

So: **no overhaul needed** — the SFX side is already the pattern I'd recommend. If there's a specific card whose SFX timing or mixing feels off, point me at it and I'll dig into that one directly rather than restructuring the whole system.

**Claude:** ## Summary

Checked every VFX controller in the project against the `CardSfxCue` + `CardSfxPlayer` pattern. Found exactly the four you predicted, no more:

**Migrated from `MMF_Player`/`PlayFeedbacks()` to `CardSfxCue`/`CardSfxPlayer`:**
- **Siren** — was pointing at a raw `Siren Song.wav` clip via its own `MMF_Sound` feedback; that clip was already registered in the shared `PL_Sfx` playlist as `"siren song "`, so migrated to reference it directly.
- **Kraken** — same situation, clip already in `PL_Sfx` as `"Kraken"`.
- **Lightning** — its `MMF_Player` field was actually unassigned (no sound was playing at all). `PL_Sfx` already has a `"Lightning"` entry sitting unused, so I wired that in as a bonus.
- **Hail Storm** — same as Lightning: unassigned, and `PL_Sfx` already had a matching `"HailStorm"` entry, now wired in.

All four had their now-orphaned `MMF_Player` fields/components removed. Live-verified in Play mode: all four `CardSfxCue`s resolve to the correct playlist/song and play without exceptions.

**Two adjacent bugs found during the audit (not the original ask, but directly relevant — silent SFX):**
1. **Three effects had real SFX data authored but never actually triggered it**: Treasure Chest ("Treasure"), Monkey Grab ("Monkey"), and Recon Parrot (random-from-playlist) each had a `CardPresentationEntry.Sfx` cue assigned in their CardSO, but their `ICardPlayEffect` controllers never called `context.PlaySfx` — so the sound was silently dropped every time, regardless of correct data. Fixed by invoking `context.PlaySfx` at the right beat in each (coin burst, the monkey's vanish/"grab" moment, and the parrot's arrival before the reveal panel).
2. **A separate, more widespread data bug**: 9 CardSO assets (Pistol, Cannonball, Chain Shot, Torch, Whale Ram, Treasure Chest, Recon Parrot, Monkey Grab, Essence Plunder) had `_volumeMultiplier: 0` / `_pitchMultiplier: 0` baked into their presentation entry — a classic Unity quirk where fields added to a class *after* an asset was last saved backfill to the CLR default (`0`) instead of the C# field initializer (`1f`). A multiplier of 0 means silence even if everything else is wired correctly. Reset all 9 to `1`/`1`. (Most of these — Pistol/Cannonball/Chain Shot/Torch/Whale Ram — don't actually consume this field today since they use their own dedicated per-controller SFX fields instead, but fixing it removes a landmine for whenever that entry data does get wired up.)

Only remaining known gap: **Essence Plunder's** entry still has no playlist assigned at all (`_playlist: {fileID: 0}`) — nothing in `PL_Sfx` obviously fits "mana drain," so I left that for you to pick a clip rather than guessing.

Zero compile errors/warnings throughout, and everything was live-verified via direct `CardSfxPlayer.Play` calls rather than just static inspection.

**Claude:** Here's the commit message for everything currently uncommitted — not committing, per your instruction:

**Title:**
```
Fix screen shake, SFX architecture, card interaction bugs, and draw-phase rules
```

**Body:**
```
Fix screen shake, SFX architecture, card interaction bugs, and draw-phase rules

- Screen shake was landing near-zero on roughly 1 in 5 hits: MMWiggle's
  Noise mode randomizes its own effective amplitude once per trigger
  between -amplitude and +amplitude. Replaced MMCameraShaker/MMWiggle
  with a small deterministic shake driver (same MMCameraShakeEvent API,
  so existing MMF_CameraShake feedbacks keep working), boosted the
  preset amplitudes, and unified Cannonball/Pistol/Chain Shot/Tidal
  Wave/Whale Ram onto the shared ScreenShake preset system instead of
  scattered ad-hoc per-controller values.
- Migrated Siren, Kraken, Lightning, and Hail Storm off ad-hoc MMF_Player
  sound feedbacks onto the shared CardSfxCue/CardSfxPlayer pattern used
  by every other card, reusing clips already sitting in the shared
  playlist. Also fixed Treasure Chest, Monkey Grab, and Recon Parrot,
  whose SFX cues were authored but never actually invoked, and reset a
  batch of CardSO presentation entries whose volume/pitch multipliers
  had silently backfilled to 0 (a Unity newly-added-field quirk).
- Fixed a pooling bug where a card dragged and released (but not played)
  could come back non-interactive on a future draw: the reaction-charge
  absorb animation left CanvasGroup.blocksRaycasts disabled on the
  pooled CardView and never restored it.
- Fixed hover/drag/layout tweens capturing a mid-animation position or
  scale as their "base" when they overlapped, which could compound into
  a card getting visibly stuck enlarged or drifted after rapid
  interactions — every such tween now completes any in-flight tween
  before reading current values.
- Fixed the enemy's Monkey Grab steal leaving the stolen card at the
  wrong on-screen height: RefreshEnemyLayout preserved whatever Y a
  card already had instead of snapping to the enemy hand's fixed
  baseline, which broke for a card reparented in from the player's hand.
- Fixed reaction cards (Dead Man's Turn, Counter Gale) not counting
  toward a turn's draw quota, so drawing N cards where some were
  reactions no longer over-draws to compensate — applied consistently
  to the player's and enemy's draw phases and the opening hand deal.
- Brought the enemy's use of Dead Man's Turn and Counter Gale up to the
  same rules as the player's: HP cost + mana surcharge on Dead Man's
  Turn, mana refund + card draw on Counter Gale.
- Dead Man's Turn VFX now recoils the actual evading ship (with the
  anchor icon parented to it) instead of a standalone floating sprite,
  pausing the ship's idle oscillation for the duration.
- Added an adjustable vertical offset for Tidal Wave's VFX graphic.
- Map ship icon now flips to face its actual direction of travel.
- Replaced all em dashes with regular hyphens across every project
  script and doc (comments and string literals alike).
```

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Route-chain waypoint architecture** for the map's ship travel: a fixed `RouteOrder = { Port, Level1, Level2, Level3 }` array lets any point-to-point trip be decomposed into consecutive adjacent "legs," each contributing its own 2 configured waypoints, so multi-hop trips (e.g., Port→Level3) naturally pass through intermediate nodes and their legs' waypoints rather than needing a combinatorial 6-pair waypoint set.
   - **DOTween `DOPath` with `PathType.CatmullRom`** used on `RectTransform.position` (not `anchoredPosition`) directly, since `RectTransform` inherits `Transform` and for a Screen Space Overlay canvas, `.position` already behaves as screen-pixel space — eliminating the need for the old `ToLocalPoint`/`RectTransformUtility` conversion dance entirely for this use case.
   - **DOTweenPro's `.OnWaypointChange(Action<int>)`** — confirmed to be a genuine, compiled feature (via `DOTweenPro.dll`, a separate precompiled binary from the base `DOTween.dll`) despite not appearing in grep of the loose `DOTween` source folder. Used to fire ship-facing-direction flips exactly when the ship passes each waypoint.
   - **Speed-based duration** instead of fixed duration: `duration = totalPathDistance / shipSpeed`, computed by summing Euclidean distances between consecutive path points (straight-line approximation of the Catmull-Rom curve length).
   - **RectTransform `anchoredPosition` vs `localPosition` vs `.position` distinction** — critical bug discovered: for a point-anchored (`anchorMin=anchorMax=0.5,0.5`) RectTransform, `manage_gameobject`'s `position`/`world_space` parameters (both on `create` and `modify`) only ever affect the serialized `m_LocalPosition` field, which Unity's UI layout system effectively ignores in favor of `m_AnchoredPosition` — meaning any attempt to position such an object via those generic Transform-style parameters silently fails to move it visually. The reliable fix is `manage_components.set_property` targeting the RectTransform component's `anchoredPosition` property directly.
   - **Deferred visual vs. instant data mutation pattern** (established convention from prior session work, being extended to Monkey Grab): `ActionEffectSO.Execute()` is fully synchronous with no async capability, so the actual GameState mutation (card ownership transfer) must always happen instantly when the card resolves — but the *visual* manifestation of that change can and should be deferred to match a VFX's own choreography, using cross-assembly delegate properties (`Systems` cannot reference `UI` directly; `GameBootstrapper` wires concrete UI callbacks onto plain `Action`/`Func` properties exposed by `Systems`-layer components).
   - **Cross-assembly delegate wiring pattern** (`Core → Data → Systems → UI → Tools`, one-way): established via `CardPresentationPlayer.ShowEnemyHandReveal { get; set; }` (a public delegate property, wired by `GameBootstrapper`) — being replicated for two new capabilities: `GetHandAreaPosition` (Func<DamageTarget, Vector3>) and `FinalizeStolenCardVisual` (Action<ICard, DamageTarget>).
   - **Event-based "learn what happened after Initialize" pattern** (established via `ReconParrotVFXController` subscribing to `GameEventBus.OnEnemyHandRevealed` in its own `Initialize()`): being replicated via a new `GameEventBus.OnCardStolen` event, since `CardPresentationPlayer` fires `FireCardPlayAccepted` (which triggers VFX `Initialize()`) *before* `CombatResolver.ResolvePlayerCard()` actually executes the card's effect — so `MonkeyGrabVFXController.Initialize()` cannot know which card was stolen until the effect resolves moments later; it must subscribe to a new event.
   - **DOTween/MCP round-trip timing quirk** (previously documented, reconfirmed this session): real wall-clock time elapses between separate `execute_code` tool calls, so short DOTween sequences frequently appear "already completed" by the next call. Worked around here via in-editor coroutines that sample state at short `WaitForSeconds` intervals within a *single* `execute_code` call.
   - **Scene-load side effects contaminating live tests**: calling the real `MoveShipThenLoad` method (which ends in `SceneFader.LoadScene`) during a sampling test caused confusing/nonsensical position readings after the scene actually changed — resolved by replicating the DOPath logic manually (without the scene-load `OnComplete`) for pure curve-shape verification.
   - **Extension-method resolution in ad-hoc `execute_code` snippets**: since `execute_code` compiles a bare method body (no ability to add `using` directives), extension methods like `.DOPath()` or `.OnWaypointChange()` fail to resolve via normal dot-syntax; worked around by calling them as fully-qualified static methods (e.g., `DG.Tweening.ShortcutExtensions.DOPath(ship, ...)`) — this is a test-harness-only limitation, not a bug in the real compiled game code (confirmed by a forced recompile showing 0 errors).
   - **Quadratic Bezier bow-curve waypoint placement**: for the map screen's 6 new waypoints, computed as points at t=1/3 and t=2/3 along a quadratic Bezier from each leg's start/end anchor `.position`, with the control point offset perpendicular to the straight line by a small "bow" magnitude (40-50 units) to create a gentle curve rather than a straight cut.

     ```csharp
     // Steals a random card from whoever did NOT cast this card, into the caster's own hand -
     // works for either side so Monkey Grab behaves correctly when the enemy plays it too.
     public void StealFromEnemyHand()
     {
         if (Caster == DamageTarget.Player)
         {
             var enemyHand = _gameState.EnemyHand.CardsSO;
             if (enemyHand.Count == 0) return;

             int    index = UnityEngine.Random.Range(0, enemyHand.Count);
             CardSO card  = enemyHand[index];
             _gameState.EnemyHand.RemoveCard(card);
             _gameState.PlayerHand.AddCard(card, _gameState.PlayerDeck.Count);
             _handLayout.StealCardFromEnemyHand(card);
             GameEventBus.FireCardDrawn(card);

         else
         {
             var playerHand = _gameState.PlayerHand.CardsSO;
             if (playerHand.Count == 0) return;

             int    index = UnityEngine.Random.Range(0, playerHand.Count);
             CardSO card  = playerHand[index];
             _gameState.PlayerHand.RemoveCard(card);
             _gameState.EnemyHand.AddCard(card, _gameState.EnemyDeck.Count);
             _handLayout.StealCardFromPlayerHand(card);
         }
     }
     ```

5. Problem Solving:
   - Solved the map's "how does the ship travel look natural along a coastline instead of cutting straight lines" problem via a maintainable route-chain design (4-node fixed order, 2 waypoints per adjacent leg, automatic concatenation for multi-hop trips) rather than a combinatorially expensive point-to-point waypoint set for all 6 possible node pairs — explicitly reasoned through and chosen as the most maintainable interpretation of "2 more steps for each path."
   - Solved smoothness via switching from chained straight-line `DOAnchorPos` segments (which produced visible "stop-and-turn" snaps at each waypoint) to a single continuous `DOPath` with `PathType.CatmullRom`, which flows naturally through all waypoints.
   - Solved speed-adjustability by replacing a fixed per-trip duration with a `_shipSpeed` (units/sec) field and computing duration from actual path length — so longer/shorter trips take proportionally longer/shorter time at a constant felt speed, and the speed itself is a single exposed Inspector value.
   - Diagnosed and fixed a real, confirmed RectTransform positioning bug in the MCP tooling itself (anchoredPosition vs localPosition) rather than assuming the waypoints were simply misplaced by design — verified via raw file inspection, not just tool response trust.
   - Currently mid-design/mid-implementation of the Monkey Grab deferred-visual architecture; the cross-assembly delegate + event-based "learn what happened later" pattern is a direct, deliberate reuse of two DISTINCT previously-established patterns in this codebase (Recon Parrot's event-subscription-in-Initialize, and Essence Plunder/Treasure Chest's deferred-visual-via-delegate), chosen specifically because they're proven, idiomatic solutions for this exact class of problem (VFX needing information or capabilities that only exist in a different assembly or become available only after Initialize() has already run).

**You:** how will the ship move if going from level 3 to port?
  - `Read: C:\Unity Projects\ThroneOfTides\Assets\_Game\2. Scripts\UI\LevelSelectManager.cs`

**Claude:** Going from Level 3 to Port is a 3-leg trip (Level3→Level2→Level1→Port), and the code walks it as one continuous curve rather than three separate hops.

`BuildRoute` decomposes it via the fixed `RouteOrder = [Port, Level1, Level2, Level3]`, stepping backward from index 3 to index 0. It concatenates, in order:
1. Level2↔Level3 leg's waypoints, reversed (`WaypointB → WaypointA`), then the Level 2 node anchor itself
2. Level1↔Level2 leg's waypoints, reversed, then the Level 1 node anchor
3. Port↔Level1 leg's waypoints, reversed (`WaypointB → WaypointA → PortMidwayAnchor`), then the Port anchor

That gives one 10-point list, fed as a single `DOPath` with `PathType.CatmullRom` — so the ship sails one smooth curve that happens to pass directly through the Level 2 and Level 1 nodes on its way home, rather than snapping/stopping at each one. `OnWaypointChange` flips the ship's facing sprite at each of those points based on which way the x-coordinate is heading next. Duration is the summed straight-line length of all those segments divided by `_shipSpeed`, so the 3-leg trip naturally takes about 3x as long as a single-leg one, then the usual `_arrivalDelay` pause before the Port scene loads.

**Claude:** Clean compile. To summarize the fix:

- **Root cause of the "flew right and vanished"**: `context.GetHandAreaPosition(...)` returns a UI RectTransform's `.position`, which on a Screen Space Overlay canvas is already screen-pixel space — I was feeding it through `RectTransformUtility.WorldToScreenPoint(camera, ...)` as if it were a genuine 3D world point, which re-projects it through the camera and sends it to a garbage location. Added a separate `ScreenSpaceUIToCanvasLocalPoint` helper (skips the camera step) for the hand target, while the ship's real 3D world anchor still correctly goes through `WorldToCanvasLocalPoint` (camera projection included).
- **Configurable wait/speed**: the pre-flight hold (`_cardHoldDuration`) was already an Inspector field; I converted the flight itself from a fixed `_cardFlightDuration` to `_cardFlightSpeed` (canvas units/sec, default 1200) — travel time is now the actual on-screen distance divided by that speed, so it scales naturally if the ship-to-hand distance varies, and both values are tunable in the Inspector on `MonkeyGrabVFXController`.

Not yet live-tested in Play mode — worth triggering Monkey Grab again to confirm it now visibly sails from the ship into the hand area before popping in.

**Claude:** Fixed. Traced the double-shake to `CardVFXHandler`'s generic hit feedback (`FB_LightHit`/`FB_MediumHit`/`FB_HeavyHit`) — each of those `MMF_Player` bundles has its own `MMF_CameraShake` step that fires the instant `GameEventBus.OnDamageDealt` fires, i.e. the moment the card resolves (well before any thrown/traveling VFX visually lands). On top of that, 6 self-driving VFX controllers *also* call `ScreenShake.Trigger(...)` explicitly, correctly timed to their own deferred impact — so any card using one of these got shaken twice: once instantly on activation, once again on the real hit.

Added a suppression mechanism (mirrors the existing `SuppressNextManaGainPopup` pattern):

- `CardEffectSpawnContext.SuppressNextDamageCameraShake` (new delegate) → `CardVFXHandler.SuppressNextDamageCameraShake()`, which temporarily disables just the `MMF_CameraShake` step (via `GetFeedbackOfType<MMF_CameraShake>()`) before playing that hit's feedback, then re-enables it for next time.
- Called from `Initialize()` — before `CombatResolver` applies damage — in every controller that owns its own impact shake: [TorchVFXController.cs](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/Systems/VFX/TorchVFXController.cs) (only when Gunpowder is active, since that's the only branch with its own shake), [CannonballVFXController.cs](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/Systems/VFX/CannonballVFXController.cs) (Pistol/Cannonball/Chain Shot), [KrakenVFXController.cs](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/Systems/VFX/KrakenVFXController.cs), [LightningVFXController.cs](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/Systems/VFX/LightningVFXController.cs), [TidalWaveVFXController.cs](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/Systems/VFX/TidalWaveVFXController.cs), and [WhaleRamVFXController.cs](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/Systems/VFX/WhaleRamVFXController.cs).
- The suppression flag is consumed unconditionally in `OnDamageDealt` (not just when a hit-tier branch runs), so a 0-damage event — e.g. a negated Kraken-vs-Kraken standoff — can't leak the suppression into an unrelated later hit.

Every other attack card (no dedicated self-driving impact controller) keeps its single, generic on-damage shake untouched. Compiles clean; worth a Play-mode pass on Torch (with and without Gunpowder), Kraken, Lightning, Tidal Wave, Whale Ram, and Cannonball/Pistol/Chain Shot to confirm each now shakes exactly once, timed to the visual hit.

**Claude:** Scene is clean (not dirty) — everything is saved. All six requests are complete and verified:

**1. Hand size cap** — Normal draws still cap at 4 (`GameConfigSO.MaxHandSize`). Treasure Chest and Monkey Grab can push past that, but only up to a new absolute ceiling of 6 (`GameConfigSO.BonusMaxHandSize`); beyond that, the bonus card is skipped and logged via `GameEventBus.FireMatchNote`. Also fixed a real bug along the way: Monkey Grab's steal was checking hand fullness *after* already removing the card from the victim's hand, which would have made a stolen card vanish into neither hand once the cap was hit.

**2. Starter deck corruption** — Root cause: `PortDeckEditor` mutates the live `PlayerDeck.asset` directly, and Unity doesn't revert ScriptableObject asset edits made in Play Mode the way it does scene objects — so testing the deck editor could permanently corrupt the "reset" baseline too, since it lived as a plain list on the same asset family. Fixed by creating a dedicated [StarterDeckTemplate.asset](Assets/_Game/4.%20Data/Decks/StarterDeckTemplate.asset) that nothing ever writes to, and pointing `PlayerInventory.Reset()` at it.

**3 & 4. Reaction prompt sometimes missing / Dead Man's Turn vs. Gunpowder Barrel & DOT** — Both traced to the same two bugs in `TurnCoordinator`: Siren Song's "next attack unblockable" flag was never consumed on use, so one Siren cast silently made *every* later attack that turn (and beyond) unblockable, locking out DMT/Counter Gale even with charges — fixed via `ConsumeSirenIfActive`. Separately, Gunpowder Barrel (priming) and DOT cards resolved and applied their effect before any reaction check ever ran, so DMT could never dodge them — added a dedicated DMT-only reaction path (`ResolveReactableZeroDamageCard`) that checks *before* resolving, with no Counter Gale option (matches your rule).

**5 & 6. Cheat panels** — Added a name-search box to the existing card-add panel, and built a new toggleable "Force Enemy" panel (same scroll+search layout, Reaction cards excluded) that guarantees the enemy plays your chosen card next via `TurnCoordinator.ForceEnemyToPlayCard`.

Live-verified all of it in Play mode: both panels toggle, populate (21 vs. 19 cards), search-filter correctly, and the hand-cap/force-play logs fired exactly as expected.

**You:** reagrading the starting deck fix - is creating a dedicated StarterDeckTemplate.asset that nothing ever writes to, and pointing PlayerInventory.Reset() at it not just delaying the problem? or is the template deck copied into the active player deck?

**Claude:** Good question — let me verify precisely rather than assume, since this matters.
  - `Bash: grep -rl "51a709f4c81551e469a96ff5aae28f82" "C:/Unity Projects/ThroneOfTides/Assets" --include=*.asset --include=*.unity --include=*.prefab`
  - `Read: C:\Unity Projects\ThroneOfTides\Assets\_Game\2. Scripts\Data\PlayerInventory.cs`

**Claude:** It's copied, not referenced — confirmed both by the code and by checking that the template asset is wired nowhere else in the project. Two things worth being precise about:

**Reset() copies values, not a reference.** `DeckDefinitionSO.CardEntry` is a `struct`, so `_playerDeck.Cards.AddRange(_starterDeckTemplate.Cards)` copies each entry *by value* into `PlayerDeck.asset`'s own list. After that call, the two `List<CardEntry>` are completely independent — `PlayerDeck.asset` and `StarterDeckTemplate.asset` never share any object. Editing the live deck afterward (via the in-game deck editor) only ever touches `PlayerDeck.asset`'s list.

**The template is never wired anywhere else** — I just grepped every `.asset`/`.unity`/`.prefab` in the project for its guid, and `PlayerInventory._starterDeckTemplate` is the *only* reference that exists. It's not `_playerDeckOverride`, not an enemy deck, not in `BuildDeckProfiles.asset`. So nothing besides `Reset()` even touches it, and `Reset()` only ever reads `.Cards` off it — never assigns to it.

So this isn't delaying the problem, it's actually closing the vector: the corruption happened because `PortDeckEditor` mutates whatever asset `PlayerInventory._playerDeck` points at, and Unity doesn't revert ScriptableObject asset edits made in Play Mode. That mutation can only ever reach an asset that's *live-wired as the active deck* somewhere (as `_playerDeck`, a deck-profile override, etc.). `StarterDeckTemplate.asset` is deliberately wired into nothing except `Reset()`'s read, so there's no path by which normal play, testing, or the deck editor can ever touch it — short of someone manually opening that specific asset in the Inspector and hand-editing it, which is a human-error case no code structure can fully prevent, but is also far less likely than the "accidentally left Play Mode running while tweaking your deck" scenario that caused the original bug.

**You:** and the template is based upon the balanced starter deck you have suggested to me earlier in out chat?

**Claude:** No — I didn't design or suggest a deck composition anywhere in this conversation. I want to be precise here since it matters for trusting the reset behavior.

What I actually did: I duplicated the *existing* `PlayerDeck.asset` (the live deck asset already in the project) to create `StarterDeckTemplate.asset`. That composition — 16 distinct cards, 30 total copies — was already sitting in the project in two places before I touched anything: as `PlayerDeck.asset` itself, and as the embedded `_startingDeckCards` list on `PlayerInventoryTEMP.asset` (which matched it exactly). I treated that pre-existing, already-matching pair as good evidence of what the designer-intended "balanced starting deck" was supposed to be, and used it as the source for the new template.

So the template reflects whatever was already configured as the starting deck in the project — not a composition I invented or recommended. If that 16-card/30-copy list doesn't actually reflect the deck you consider properly balanced right now (e.g., if it had already drifted from edits before you asked me to fix the reset mechanism), the template will faithfully preserve that drift rather than correct it.

Worth you doing: open [StarterDeckTemplate.asset](Assets/_Game/4.%20Data/Decks/StarterDeckTemplate.asset) in the Inspector and check the card/count list is actually the deck you want players reset to. If it's off, edit that asset directly (safe to do — nothing else references it) and it'll take effect the next time someone hits Reset.

**Claude:** Done. Added a **Presentation Mode** button to `CheatsPanel` that sets both sides' HP and Mana (current *and* max) to 999 in one click — live-verified in Play mode, hit exactly `999/999` on all four values.

On persistence: this works purely through `GameState`'s existing per-side cheat methods (`CheatSetPlayerMaxHP` → `CheatAddPlayerHP`, etc.), the same ones the other buttons already use — nothing new needed there. That already guarantees it can't leak into the next match, because of how the architecture is structured, not because of anything special I added for this button:

- `GameState` is a plain in-memory object built fresh every time `GameBootstrapper.Start()` runs (i.e., every time the Match scene loads), with `MaxHP`/`MaxMana` computed from `GameConfigSO.StartingHP`/`StartingMaxMana` plus whatever `PlayerInventory`'s saved upgrade levels say.
- `PlayerInventory.Save()` — the only thing that actually writes to disk — is called from upgrade purchases and `Reset()`, never from `CheatsPanel`. Presentation Mode touches only the live `GameState`, so there's nothing to save even if a save happened to fire.
- The next match starts a brand-new `GameState` from those same saved upgrade levels, completely independent of whatever the previous match's `GameState` was left at — cheat-inflated or not.

So the "don't let it leak" requirement was already satisfied by the existing architecture; I didn't need to add any extra guard for it.

**Claude:** I did a full audit of every draw path (player's opening hand, player's per-turn refill, and both enemy mirrors), and the player-side logic already implements exactly what you're describing — nothing needed changing there. Let me walk through why, since you're right to want this double-checked given how many other systems shifted this session.

**[TurnCoordinator.cs:326-357](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/Systems/TurnCoordinator.cs) — `RefillPlayerHandRoutine`, the per-turn draw:**
```csharp
int drawsRemaining = _config.MaxHandSize - _gameState.PlayerHand.Count;
for (int i = 0; i < drawsRemaining && _gameState.PlayerDeck.Count > 0; i++)
{
    CardSO drawn = _gameState.PlayerDeck.Draw();
    ...
    if (drawn.CardType == CardType.Reaction)
    {
        pendingReactionCards.Add(drawn);
        ... deal it into the fanned hand like any other card ...
        continue;
    }
    _gameState.PlayerHand.AddCard(drawn, _config.MaxHandSize);
    ...
}
_gameState.SetHasDrawnThisTurn();
foreach (var card in pendingReactionCards)
    StartCoroutine(AbsorbReactionCard(card));
```

- `drawsRemaining` is computed from *current* hand count, so it never draws a blind fixed 4 — if 2 cards are already sitting in hand from last turn, it only draws 2. That's "fill up to 4," not "always exactly 4."
- The loop runs exactly `drawsRemaining` times regardless of card type — a Reaction card still consumes one iteration/one physical draw, so it occupies a "slot" during the draw phase itself. Nothing compensates by drawing an extra replacement card, which is exactly the "don't draw more than needed" behavior you're asking for.
- Reaction cards are visibly dealt into the hand alongside everything else, and only get absorbed into their badge in `AbsorbReactionCard`, called in the `foreach` *after* the whole loop and `SetHasDrawnThisTurn()` — i.e., after the draw stage is fully done, as the turn is beginning.

**[GameBootstrapper.cs:205-243](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/App/GameBootstrapper.cs) — the player's opening hand (`DealPlayerOpeningHandRoutine`):** same shape — `drawsRemaining = MaxHandSize - PlayerHand.Count`, Reaction cards go into a `reactionCards` list and get dealt into the visual hand via `dealtCards`, and only after `DealOpeningHandAnimated` finishes does it `WaitForSeconds(ReactionAbsorbDelay)` and then charge them via `AnimateReactionAbsorb`.

One asymmetry I found while auditing, for transparency: the **enemy's** two draw paths (`GameBootstrapper.DealOpeningHand` and `TurnCoordinator`'s enemy refill block) charge Reaction cards immediately inline rather than deferring, unlike both player paths. I left that alone since it's not player-facing (the enemy hand is never shown face-up, so there's no "watch it fly to the badge" moment to preserve) and you specifically asked about the player's draw stage — but flagging it in case you want it made symmetric anyway for its own sake.

**Claude:** ## Commit title

```
Overhaul map travel and Monkey Grab VFX, fix reaction/shake bugs, add cheat tools
```

## Commit description

**Map (Level Select) travel**
- Ship now sails a smooth curved route through configurable waypoints instead of straight lines between nodes, with adjustable travel speed and arrival delay.
- The Port connects to all three levels through a shared hub route (regroup point + 2 waypoints) instead of chaining through the other levels' nodes.

**Monkey Grab VFX**
- The stolen card no longer appears until the monkey is back on its own ship, then flies from there to the activating player's hand as an enlarged copy of the real card (not just its art) before shrinking into the hand.
- Fixed three bugs found while building this: wrong flight target (was mis-treating the hand's screen position as a 3D world point), the flight animation getting killed mid-flight by the monkey's own cleanup, and flight speed/wait time not being tunable.

**Combat/reaction bugs**
- Dead Man's Turn can now actually dodge Gunpowder Barrel and DOT cards (Whirlpool, Hail Storm) - previously these always landed with no way to react at all.
- Fixed Siren Song's "next attack unblockable" not being consumed after use, which could silently make every later attack that turn (and beyond) unblockable and lock out reactions even with charges available - this was the cause of "reaction panel doesn't show despite having charges."
- Fixed a double screen-shake on cards with a delayed VFX impact (Torch, Cannonball, Kraken, Lightning, Tidal Wave, Whale Ram) - one instant shake fired the moment the card resolved, another fired again on the real visual hit. Torch specifically no longer shakes at all on a non-igniting throw.
- Replaced Unity's built-in camera shaker (which randomized its own strength per hit, sometimes landing near zero) with a deterministic one, and rebalanced shake strength across the board so hits actually read.

**Hand size and starting deck**
- Player hand is capped at 4 normally; Treasure Chest and Monkey Grab can push past that but never above 6, with skipped draws logged instead of silently lost. Also fixed Monkey Grab losing a stolen card entirely when the receiving hand was full.
- Added a dedicated, never-edited starter deck template asset so resetting player data reliably restores the real starting deck, instead of the previous setup, which could get silently corrupted by editing the deck during Play Mode testing.

**Cheats**
- Added a name-search box to the existing "add card to hand" cheat panel.
- Added a new toggleable panel to force the enemy to play a specific card next (same scroll+search layout).
- Added a "Presentation Mode" button that maxes and fully fills both sides' HP/mana for screenshots/demos - purely in-memory, never saved, so it can't affect a future match's starting stats.

**SFX cleanup**
- Migrated Siren, Kraken, Lightning, and Hail Storm off the old ad-hoc FEEL player pattern onto the shared card-SFX system; fixed Treasure Chest, Monkey Grab, and Recon Parrot never actually playing their configured sound; fixed 9 cards with silently-zeroed volume/pitch.

**Text cleanup**
- Replaced em dashes with regular dashes across card descriptions, UI text, and code comments/docs.

---

To commit as-is:

```bash
git add -A
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Overhaul map travel and Monkey Grab VFX, fix reaction/shake bugs, add cheat tools

Map (Level Select) travel:
- Ship now sails a smooth curved route through configurable waypoints instead of straight lines between nodes, with adjustable travel speed and arrival delay.
- The Port connects to all three levels through a shared hub route (regroup point + 2 waypoints) instead of chaining through the other levels' nodes.

Monkey Grab VFX:
- The stolen card no longer appears until the monkey is back on its own ship, then flies from there to the activating player's hand as an enlarged copy of the real card before shrinking into the hand.
- Fixed wrong flight target, the animation being killed mid-flight, and non-configurable flight speed/wait time.

Combat/reaction bugs:
- Dead Man's Turn can now dodge Gunpowder Barrel and DOT cards, which previously always landed with no way to react.
- Fixed Siren Song's unblockable flag never being consumed, which could lock out reactions entirely even with charges available.
- Fixed a double screen-shake on cards with delayed VFX impact (Torch, Cannonball, Kraken, Lightning, Tidal Wave, Whale Ram).
- Replaced Unity's camera shaker with a deterministic one and rebalanced shake strength across the board.

Hand size and starting deck:
- Player hand capped at 4 normally, up to 6 via Treasure Chest/Monkey Grab, with skipped draws logged. Fixed Monkey Grab losing a stolen card when the hand was full.
- Added a dedicated starter deck template asset so Reset Player Data reliably restores the real starting deck.

Cheats:
- Added search to the card-add cheat panel.
- Added a new panel to force the enemy to play a specific card next.
- Added a Presentation Mode button (999 HP/mana both sides, in-memory only).

SFX cleanup:
- Migrated Siren/Kraken/Lightning/Hail Storm to the shared card-SFX system; fixed Treasure Chest/Monkey Grab/Recon Parrot never playing their SFX; fixed 9 cards with zeroed volume/pitch.

Text cleanup:
- Replaced em dashes with regular dashes across card descriptions, UI text, and code/docs.
EOF
)"
```

**You:** how to create a reverse cone shaped particle system in unit 6.3 to emulate a suction effect (large area into a point

**Claude:** Unity MCP just disconnected on my end, so I can't build this directly in your project right now — here's how to do it by hand in the Inspector (this is unchanged from any recent Unity version; "6.3" doesn't add anything new to the Shuriken Particle System for this).

## The core trick

A cone `Shape` module normally spawns particles at the tip and sends them flying outward toward the wide end. For suction, you want the opposite: spawn particles across the wide end and pull them toward the tip. You get that by keeping the cone shape exactly as-is and driving motion with a **negative Z force/velocity in Local space** instead of the cone's own outward `Start Speed`.

## Step by step

1. **Create it**: `GameObject > Effects > Particle System`.
2. **Main module**:
   - `Start Speed = 0` (don't let the cone's own outward speed fight your pull).
   - `Simulation Space = Local` (so the pull direction stays relative to the cone even if you move/rotate the whole system).
   - `Start Lifetime` ~0.5–1s — this doubles as your "travel time" to the point, so tune it alongside the force strength below.
3. **Shape module**:
   - `Shape = Cone`.
   - `Angle` — wider angle = wider mouth of the suction area (try 20–40°).
   - `Radius` — controls how big the "large area" is.
   - `Emit From = Volume` (fills the whole cone, not just the surface) for a denser look.
   - `Arc = 360` for full radial coverage.
   - Leave rotation at default — the cone's **tip is your suction point**, the wide end (+Z by default) is the "large area."
4. **Velocity over Lifetime** (or **Force over Lifetime** — see note below):
   - Enable it, set `Space = Local`.
   - Set **Linear Z to a negative value** — this pulls particles from the wide end back toward the tip.

   **Force over Lifetime vs. Velocity over Lifetime**: Force accelerates (starts slow, speeds up as it gets sucked in — reads much more like real suction/gravity-well pull). Velocity moves at constant speed toward the tip (simpler, more mechanical-looking). For a convincing "suction" feel, prefer **Force over Lifetime** with local `-Z`.
5. **Size over Lifetime**: curve from 1 → 0, so particles shrink to nothing right as they reach the point — sells the "disappearing into a point" illusion even if they slightly overshoot.
6. **Color over Lifetime** (optional): fade alpha to 0 near the end as a backup/blend with the size shrink.
7. **Noise module** (optional): add mild strength for organic, non-mechanical drift — or use the **Orbital X/Y/Z** fields under Velocity over Lifetime to add a swirl, which gives you a "drain/vortex" look instead of straight-line suction.
8. **Emission**: `Rate over Time` controls how dense the effect reads across the wide area.
9. **Renderer**: billboard alignment; an additive-blend material usually sells energy/suction effects better than alpha-blended.

**Claude:** Found and fixed the real bug. In [TurnCoordinator.cs](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/Systems/TurnCoordinator.cs) (both `RefillPlayerHandRoutine` and the enemy's per-turn refill) and [GameBootstrapper.cs](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/App/GameBootstrapper.cs) (both opening-hand deals), the "how many cards to draw" calculation only looked at hand count:

```csharp
int drawsRemaining = _config.MaxHandSize - _gameState.PlayerHand.Count;
```

Reaction charges (Dead Man's Turn / Counter Gale) never get consumed on their own — only by actually firing the reaction in combat — so they're a resource that just keeps accumulating turn after turn. Since the old formula didn't count them, every turn where you'd drawn some reaction cards in the past kept refilling your *hand* back to 4 on top of whatever charges you'd already banked, letting the true total climb indefinitely (6 hand + 2 charges = 8, matching what you saw). Fixed to count both:

```csharp
int currentTotal   = _gameState.PlayerHand.Count + _gameState.PlayerDeadMansTurnCharges + _gameState.PlayerCounterGaleCharges;
int drawsRemaining = _config.MaxHandSize - currentTotal;
```

Applied the same fix symmetrically to the enemy's refill, and to both opening-hand deals for formula consistency (a no-op there today since charges start at 0, but keeps all four draw sites using the same rule).

Verified across 4 real turns in Play mode — played cards, let the enemy act (including it casting Monkey Grab and stealing a card from me), and checked hand+charges after every refill: total was capped at exactly 4 every single time, with every card-count change traceable to an actual game event rather than a runaway draw.

Modified `BuildDevelopment()` in [ThroneOfTidesBuildPipeline.cs](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/Tools/Build/ThroneOfTidesBuildPipeline.cs) — it's the only build type of the four that no longer calls `ApplySceneOverrides`:

- **Before**: even the "Development" build silently forced `Match.unity`'s player/enemy deck references to whatever `BuildDeckProfiles.asset` had configured for that profile type, then reverted it after — meaning what actually got built could differ from what you had open and configured in the Editor.
- **Now**: it builds `Match.unity` exactly as currently authored — whatever decks are wired into `GameBootstrapper`, whatever active/inactive state the `CheatsPanel`/`CardCheatPanel`/`ForceEnemyCardCheatPanel` GameObjects are already in. No backup/restore step needed since nothing gets mutated.

Cheats specifically: they don't actually depend on this override logic at all — each panel's `Awake()` only hides itself when `!Debug.isDebugBuild`, and `BuildOptions.Development` (which this build type already used) keeps that flag true. So cheats show up as long as you haven't explicitly deactivated their GameObjects in the scene, regardless of this pipeline change — this fix is really about the deck-swap side effect, not cheat visibility (which already worked correctly).

`Release`, `Playtest Config`, and `WebGL` builds are untouched — they still intentionally apply their own overrides (Release disables cheats, Playtest bumps HP/hand size, etc.), since those are presumably still wanted.

One thing I didn't touch: the `BuildProfileType.Development` enum entry and its corresponding row in `BuildDeckProfiles.asset` are now unused dead data. I left them in place rather than removing them, since Unity serializes that enum by ordinal position — deleting the entry would shift `Release`/`Playtest`/`WebGL`'s stored integer values and could silently scramble which profile is which. Harmless as-is, but worth knowing it's there if you ever clean up that asset.

**Claude:** Nothing to save (scene not dirty — only code was touched). Here's what I found and fixed:

**Was my earlier fix actually correct?** Mostly, but with a real gap you were right to push on. Tracing through the old code: when the hand is already above 4 (e.g., 6 from a Treasure Chest), the count-computed-once formula gives a *negative* `drawsRemaining`, so the loop wouldn't run at all — that part was already correct. But there was a genuine hole your suggestion exposed: the loop's count was computed **once** up front and never re-checked. If a *reaction card* was drawn, it doesn't get added to the hand or its charge counter immediately — it sits in limbo (visually dealt, but not counted anywhere) until a separate delayed step charges it *after* the whole loop finishes. That's harmless for a fixed-iteration loop, but it's exactly the kind of thing that could go wrong in edge cases and is worth being defensive about.

**What I changed** ([TurnCoordinator.cs](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/Systems/TurnCoordinator.cs)) — implemented exactly what you asked: both the player's and enemy's refill now use a `while` loop that re-checks the live total (hand + charges, plus any reaction cards drawn *this* loop that haven't been charged yet) after every single card, instead of trusting a count computed at the start:

```csharp
while (_gameState.PlayerHand.Count + _gameState.PlayerDeadMansTurnCharges + _gameState.PlayerCounterGaleCharges + pendingReactionCards.Count < _config.MaxHandSize
       && _gameState.PlayerDeck.Count > 0)
```

**Verified live**, reproducing your exact scenario: forced the hand to 6 (simulating a Treasure Chest overflow), then ran a full turn cycle through the real UI (End Turn → enemy turn → back to player). Result: hand stayed at exactly 6, zero cards drawn.

One thing worth being explicit about, since it's the crux of what you were asking: **the fix guarantees the draw phase never *adds* cards once you're at or above 4** — but it does **not** forcibly discard existing excess. If Treasure Chest pushed you to 6, the next turn's draw correctly draws 0, but the hand stays at 6 until *you* play cards down below 4 — only then does the next refill top it back up toward 4. If what you actually want is cards being auto-discarded down to 4 at some point, that's a different, deliberate design decision (and a bit unusual for a card game) — let me know if that's really what you meant and I'll implement it separately.

i was not drawing when i had only 3 cards in hand - why?

**You:** This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:

This is a long-running Unity/C# development session for "Throne of Tides" (C:\Unity Projects\ThroneOfTides), a 2D pirate-ship card-battler, worked on via UnityMCP tools. The user's requests in this visible window, in chronological order:

1. **"create a reverse cone shaped particle system in unit 6.3 to emulate a suction effect (large area into a point"** — general Unity knowledge question (answered without tools, MCP was disconnected at the time).
2. **"create one like that in the match scene"** — build the suction particle system for real, in the Match scene. COMPLETED, then iterated:
   - **"it si not looking like a suction effect at all man. we are in 2d"** — root cause: cone's collapse axis (local Z) pointed along the camera's view axis (orthographic camera looking down Z), invisible in 2D. Fixed by rotating 90° so collapse happens in visible XY plane. Then also had to scale up the whole effect (too subtle at real camera zoom).
3. **"make the essence plunder aprticle effect appear ont the activating player's ship unlike what we have right now"** — traced to a backwards Force-over-Lifetime Y sign in `EssencePlunderManaFlowParticles.prefab`, causing mana to visually flow AWAY from the caster instead of toward them. Fixed by flipping sign.
4. **"make so i can choose where the particle effect is spawned (on which ship , directed at the other ship automatically)"** — added a `ManaFlowOrigin` enum (Opponent/Caster) to `EssencePlunderVFXController`, defaulting to Opponent (preserving old behavior), with both ends resolved relative to caster so it's automatically correct either way.
5. **"the vfx controller is asking for only 1 particle system prefab - but the parent dosnt have a particle system, its empty just to hold the 3 children with particle systems on them - maybe get them dynamically? or is it bad for performence"** — user had restructured the prefab themselves (root now empty Transform-only, 3 children "Left"/"Center"/"Right" each with own ParticleSystem). Confirmed dynamic lookup via `GetComponentsInChildren<ParticleSystem>()` is correct and NOT a performance concern (fires once per card play, not per-frame). Changed `_manaFlowParticlesPrefab` field type from `ParticleSystem` to `GameObject`, re-wired the prefab reference (lost due to type change), updated `_particleInstance` field type, and `OnParticleComplete`'s Destroy call.
6. **"the alntern should stay and not dissappear until the particle effect is done, wait a bit (0.2-0.3 seconds) and then fade out. also - for some reason the effect is not visible... i think because of placement in the scene world space or position in the prefab"** — added `_postParticleHoldDuration` (0.25f default) hold before fade-out; found and fixed the real visibility bug: each of the 3 children's Shape module had a large `position` offset (~±2, -3.25/-6.7, 0) baked in, displacing actual particle emission several units away from the ship. Reset all three to `(0,0,0)`.
7. **"one bug that is still up - sometimes on the later turns while having 3-4 cards in hand i still draw 4 cards in teh draw phase causing overflow of the hand size beyond the intended 4 at the bginning of the turn - prevent this please" + "also, add a sfx slot for the tidal wave vfx at the start of it with a short delay"** — two separate asks, both made as file edits while Unity MCP was disconnected:
   - Traced draw overflow to a deck-click race: `RefillPlayerHandRoutine` only set `HasDrawnThisTurn = true` at the END of the loop, but nothing disabled deck clicks during the multi-card animation window, so a manual `TryDrawCard()` click could sneak in an extra draw. Fixed by moving `SetHasDrawnThisTurn()` earlier.
   - Added `_startSfx`/`_startSfxDelay` fields to `TidalWaveVFXController`, scheduled via `_sequence.InsertCallback(_startSfxDelay, ...)` so it plays independently alongside the fill/move animation.
8. **"make sure the port scene is included in the develpoment build and the rest of what we said"** — found `Port.unity` missing from `ThroneOfTidesBuildPipeline.cs`'s hardcoded `Scenes` array (used by all custom build menu items), even though Unity's own Build Settings already had it correctly ordered (MainMenu → LevelSelect → Port → Match). Fixed. Also asked to verify/complete "the rest of what we said" — triggered re-verification of the draw-overflow fix and Tidal Wave SFX addition now that Unity MCP had reconnected; during this verification, discovered the earlier draw fix was incomplete (see Errors and Fixes).
9. **"are you sure i cant have more than 4 cards in my hand post draw? its fine to have more than 5 mid turn if you stole cards from the enemy or used a treasure chest, but i still remain after the turn after's draw with more than 4 cards in hand. maybe add a check after each drawn card how many cards are in hand? to avoid keeping on drawing if there are 4 in hand"** — MOST RECENT request. Required re-examining whether the draw-count formula could ever result in >4 total. Found the formula itself was already mathematically sound for the simple case, but implemented the user's explicitly-requested defensive per-card recheck anyway (correctly accounting for a subtlety: Reaction cards are deferred and don't count toward `PlayerHand.Count`/charges until after the whole loop finishes via `AbsorbReactionCard`, so `pendingReactionCards.Count` must be added to the running total check to avoid a different bug the naive recheck would introduce). Applied to both player and enemy per-turn refills. Live-verified: forced hand to 6 (simulating Treasure Chest overflow), ran a full turn cycle, confirmed draw phase adds exactly 0 cards and hand stays flat at 6 (not growing further) — this is by design; excess only reduces when the player plays cards down, it doesn't auto-discard.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Reverse-cone "suction" particle system technique**: `ParticleSystemShapeType.ConeVolume`, `Start Speed = 0`, `Force over Lifetime` in Local space along the shape's own axis to pull particles from a wide area to a point (or vice versa for repulsion). In Unity's 2D orthographic setup, the cone's natural collapse axis (local Z) must be rotated into the camera's visible plane (XY) since Z-axis motion produces zero visible change under orthographic projection.
   - **`ParticleSystem.Simulate(t, withChildren, restart)`** — used for deterministic mid-life sampling of particle systems during automated testing, bypassing real-time animation waiting.
   - **DOTween `Sequence.InsertCallback(atTime, callback)`** — schedules a callback at an absolute time offset within a sequence's timeline, independent of the Append/Join chain, useful for firing an SFX cue at a fixed delay without affecting other animation timing.
   - **DOTween extension method resolution in `execute_code` snippets**: `.Complete()`, `.IsActive()`, etc. require `using DG.Tweening;` which can't be added in ad-hoc snippet bodies — must call fully-qualified static forms like `DG.Tweening.TweenExtensions.Complete(seq, true)`.
   - **Unity Play Mode state reversion**: GameObjects/values existing BEFORE Play Mode starts are included in the pre-play snapshot and correctly restored on Stop; changes made DURING Play Mode to already-existing scene objects are reverted on Stop (unlike ScriptableObject *assets*, which do NOT revert).
   - **CRITICAL BUG PATTERN DISCOVERED THIS SESSION: forcing a script recompile (`refresh_unity` with `scope: scripts`, `mode: force`) while Unity is in Play Mode triggers a domain reload mid-play that corrupts the live session** — causes "The referenced script (Unknown) on this Behaviour is missing!" warnings and repeating `NullReferenceException`s every frame. Fix: always `manage_editor stop` before requesting a script compile; if corruption already occurred, reload the affected scene fresh from disk via `manage_scene load` (not just Stop/Play again, since the in-memory scene state itself was corrupted, not just the play session).
   - **Unity coroutine execution model as a hard guarantee**: C# coroutines run synchronously from invocation up to their first `yield` statement, all within the same frame/call stack — meaning code placed before any `yield` in a coroutine is guaranteed to execute before Unity's event loop can process any other event (like a UI button click), making such placement a mathematically airtight fix for UI-interaction races, not merely a probabilistic one.
   - **Deferred vs. immediate reaction-charging pattern**: player-side reaction card draws are deferred (dealt into hand visually via `pendingReactionCards` list, NOT added to `_gameState.PlayerHand`, and only converted to a badge charge via `AbsorbReactionCard` coroutine AFTER the whole draw loop finishes) — this is intentional so the reaction card "reads exactly like any other card" during the deal animation before flying off to its badge. Enemy-side reaction draws are charged IMMEDIATELY inline (no deferred visual beat, since enemy hand is never shown face-up).
   - **Hand-size invariant**: `MaxHandSize` (4) is meant to cap "total held resources" = hand cards + already-charged Dead Man's Turn/Counter Gale reaction charges, NOT bare hand count alone, since charges are a persistent match-long resource that never self-reduces.
   - **`BonusMaxHandSize` (6)** — the absolute ceiling that guaranteed bonus draws (Treasure Chest, Monkey Grab) can push a hand past the normal 4, established in an earlier (pre-summary) part of this session.
   - **Unity's custom `ThroneOfTidesBuildPipeline`** (Editor-only, `IPreprocessBuildWithReport`/`IPostprocessBuildWithReport`) with 4 menu-driven build types (Development, Release, Playtest Config, WebGL), each using a shared hardcoded `Scenes` array independent of Unity's own Build Settings (`EditorBuildSettings.scenes`) — meaning the two can silently drift out of sync (confirmed this session: Port.unity was in Build Settings but missing from the pipeline's own array).
   - **`BuildProfileType` enum (Development, Release, Playtest, WebGL)** in `BuildDeckProfileSO.cs` — serialized by ordinal position in Unity, so removing/reordering values would silently corrupt `BuildDeckProfiles.asset`'s stored int values; left untouched even though `Development` became otherwise-unused after an earlier fix (from before this summary window) that made `BuildDevelopment()` skip `ApplySceneOverrides` entirely.

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **`Assets/_Game/2. Scripts/Systems/VFX/EssencePlunderVFXController.cs`** — heavily modified this session.
     - Added nested enum: `public enum ManaFlowOrigin { Opponent, Caster }`.
     - Added fields: `[SerializeField] private ManaFlowOrigin _manaFlowOrigin = ManaFlowOrigin.Opponent;`, `[Tooltip(...)] [SerializeField] private float _postParticleHoldDuration = 0.25f;`.
     - Changed `_manaFlowParticlesPrefab` field type from `ParticleSystem` to `GameObject` (required re-wiring the prefab reference in the Inspector via `manage_components.set_property`, since Unity can't auto-convert between component-reference and GameObject-reference serialization).
     - Changed `_particleInstance` field type from `ParticleSystem` to `GameObject`.
     - Current `PlayManaFlowParticle()` body (final state):
       ```csharp
       private void PlayManaFlowParticle()
       {
           float waitDuration = 0f;

           if (_manaFlowParticlesPrefab != null)
           {
               bool startsOnCaster = _manaFlowOrigin == ManaFlowOrigin.Caster;
               Vector3 from = startsOnCaster ? _context.CasterAnchor.position   : _context.OpponentAnchor.position;
               Vector3 to   = startsOnCaster ? _context.OpponentAnchor.position : _context.CasterAnchor.position;
               Vector3 direction = (to - from).normalized;

               float angle = Mathf.Atan2(direction.y, direction.x) * Mathf.Rad2Deg - 90f;

               _particleInstance = Instantiate(_manaFlowParticlesPrefab, from, Quaternion.Euler(0f, 0f, angle));
               _context.PlaySfx?.Invoke(from);

               foreach (var system in _particleInstance.GetComponentsInChildren<ParticleSystem>(true))
               {
                   system.Play();
                   float systemDuration = system.main.duration + system.main.startLifetime.constantMax;
                   waitDuration = Mathf.Max(waitDuration, systemDuration);
               }
           }

           _sequence = DOTween.Sequence();
           _sequence.AppendInterval(waitDuration);
           _sequence.OnComplete(OnParticleComplete);
       }

       private void OnParticleComplete()
       {
           if (_particleInstance != null) Destroy(_particleInstance, 2f);

           _context.SpawnManaGainedNumber?.Invoke(_manaAmountForDisplay, _context.CasterAnchor.position);

           _sequence = DOTween.Sequence();
           _sequence.AppendInterval(_postParticleHoldDuration);
           _sequence.Append(_canvasGroup.DOFade(0f, _fadeOutDuration).SetEase(_fadeOutEase));
           _sequence.OnComplete(() => Completed?.Invoke());
       }
       ```
     - Class doc comment updated to describe the empty-rig-with-multiple-children architecture and configurable origin.

   - **`Assets/_Game/3. Prefabs/VFX/Particles/EssencePlunderManaFlowParticles.prefab`** — user restructured this themselves mid-session: root is now Transform-only (no ParticleSystem), with 3 children "Left", "Center", "Right" each carrying their own `ParticleSystem`+`ParticleSystemRenderer`.
     - Fixed via `execute_code`: each child's Shape module had `shape.position` offset ~(±2, -3.25, 0) baked in — reset all three to `(0,0,0)` via `shape.position = UnityEngine.Vector3.zero;` inside a prefab stage, then `manage_prefabs save_prefab_stage`.
     - Earlier (before restructure): the single-particle-system version's `forceOverLifetime.y` was `-15` (wrong direction, pulling toward the object's own spawn anchor / opponent's ship instead of onward toward the caster) — flipped to `+15`. This fix predates the 3-child restructure but established the correct force-direction convention still honored by the current setup.

       ```csharp
       // Called at the end of each enemy turn. Short delay lets the turn
       // transition visual settle before the cards animate in.
       // Not called on turn 1 - GameBootstrapper handles the opening hand deal.
       private IEnumerator AutoDrawRoutine()
       {
           // Set here, before the settle delay below - not just before RefillPlayerHandRoutine's
           // own loop - since the deck stays clickable through this delay too, and a click here
           // would otherwise pass CanDraw()'s !HasDrawnThisTurn check the same way one during the
           // refill's own card animations would. See RefillPlayerHandRoutine's remarks.
           _gameState.SetHasDrawnThisTurn();

           yield return new WaitForSeconds(0.3f);
           yield return StartCoroutine(RefillPlayerHandRoutine());
       ```

     - **`RefillPlayerHandRoutine()`** (final state, this is the CORE fix for the most recent user request):
       ```csharp
       // Draws until the player's total held resources (hand cards + already-charged reactions)
       // reach MaxHandSize, re-checking after every single card rather than trusting a count
       // computed once up front - see the remarks inside. A Reaction card still counts as one of
       // this turn's draws even though it ends up as a badge charge instead of a hand card, so
       // drawing 4 cards where 1 is a Reaction always ends with 3 cards in hand, never with the
       // draw continuing until 4 non-Reaction cards have been found.
       private IEnumerator RefillPlayerHandRoutine()
       {
           var pendingReactionCards = new List<CardSO>();

           // Defensive duplicate - AutoDrawRoutine already sets this before calling here, closing
           // the deck-click race for its own settle delay too. Kept here as well in case this
           // routine is ever called from somewhere that doesn't already do that.
           _gameState.SetHasDrawnThisTurn();

           // Re-checked after every single card, not computed once up front - if the hand (plus
           // already-charged reactions) is already at or above MaxHandSize when this runs (e.g. a
           // Treasure Chest/Monkey Grab bonus pushed it past 4 last turn), this draws nothing at
           // all and leaves the existing total exactly as it was; it only ever comes down once
           // the player actually plays cards. pendingReactionCards.Count is added in because a
           // reaction card drawn THIS loop sits in neither PlayerHand nor the charge counters yet
           // (it only becomes a charge once AbsorbReactionCard runs, after the whole loop below
           // finishes) - without counting it here too, several reactions drawn back to back would
           // each look like they hadn't used up a slot, letting the loop keep going past MaxHandSize.
           while (_gameState.PlayerHand.Count + _gameState.PlayerDeadMansTurnCharges + _gameState.PlayerCounterGaleCharges + pendingReactionCards.Count < _config.MaxHandSize
                  && _gameState.PlayerDeck.Count > 0)
           {
               CardSO drawn = _gameState.PlayerDeck.Draw();
               if (drawn == null) break;

               if (drawn.CardType == CardType.Reaction)
               {
                   pendingReactionCards.Add(drawn);
                   GameEventBus.FireCardDrawn(drawn);
                   OnCardDrawn?.Invoke(drawn);
                   yield return StartCoroutine(_handLayout.AnimateManualDraw(drawn));
                   continue;
               }

               _gameState.PlayerHand.AddCard(drawn, _config.MaxHandSize);
               GameEventBus.FireCardDrawn(drawn);
               OnCardDrawn?.Invoke(drawn);
               yield return StartCoroutine(_handLayout.AnimateManualDraw(drawn));
           }

           foreach (var card in pendingReactionCards)
               StartCoroutine(AbsorbReactionCard(card));
       }
       ```
     - **Enemy per-turn refill** (inside `EnemyTurnRoutine()`, final state):
       ```csharp
       // The enemy hand fully refills at the start of its turn too, mirroring the player -
       // drawing until its total held resources (hand + already-charged reactions) reach
       // MaxHandSize, re-checked after every card rather than computed once up front - see
       // RefillPlayerHandRoutine's remarks. Unlike the player's version, the enemy charges a
       // drawn Reaction immediately (no deferred "sits in hand, then flies to badge" beat to
       // account for), so the total is always accurate mid-loop with no extra bookkeeping.
       // EnemyAI.PickCard never plays Reaction-type cards, so leaving one in hand would
       // strand it there permanently unplayable.
       while (_gameState.EnemyHand.Count + _gameState.EnemyDeadMansTurnCharges + _gameState.EnemyCounterGaleCharges < _config.MaxHandSize
              && _gameState.EnemyDeck.Count > 0)
       {
           CardSO enemyDrawn = _gameState.EnemyDeck.Draw();
           if (enemyDrawn == null) break;

           if (enemyDrawn.CardType == CardType.Reaction)
           {
               ChargeReaction(enemyDrawn, DamageTarget.Enemy);
               continue;
           }

           _gameState.EnemyHand.AddCard(enemyDrawn, _config.MaxHandSize);
           _handLayout.AddCardToEnemyHand(enemyDrawn);
       }
       ```

<result>## Throne of Tides — Balance &amp; Systems Review

**Scope note:** All numbers below are read directly from `GameConfigSO.asset`, the `CardSO`/`CaptainSO`/`DeckDefinitionSO`/`UpgradeSO`/`LevelRewardSO` asset instances, and the effect/resolver/AI source files.

### (A) Card-by-card power notes

- **Lightning** (4 mana, 10 dmg, storage 6): best flat damage-per-mana in the flat-damage tier (2.5/mana) with zero drawback, vs. Cannonball (1/1=2.0), WhaleRam (3/6=2.0), ChainShot (2/4=2.0+upside). No HP cost, no target restriction, no combo setup required. It's a auto-include finisher with nothing else in its cost bracket competing.
- **Chain Shot** (2 mana, 4 dmg, storage 3, 50% discard-1-from-opponent-hand): strictly better than a vanilla 4-damage card at the same cost — the discard is pure upside with no cost, RNG-gated but free. No comparable 2-mana card has a stapled-on disruption effect.
- **Hail Storm** (3 mana, DOT 2×3=6 total) is dominated by **Whale Ram** (3 mana, 6 flat immediate) — same total damage, worse (delayed, interruptible by the deck running dry near match end, no upfront burst), for identical cost. **Whirlpool** (4 mana, DOT 3×3=9) similarly trails Lightning's 10-for-4 in total damage while being slower and, per `CombatResolver.ResolveDOT`, easily invalidated if the match ends before all ticks land. Both DOT cards read as weak text-based worse than raw beaters.
- **Essence Plunder** (0 mana, 3 HP cost, steal 2 mana from opponent, floor 1): a free tempo swing of roughly 2 extra mana this turn for 3 HP, with `MaxCopiesInDeck = 99` (no per-deck cap unlike Kraken's 1 or the reactions' 2). Nothing stops a deck from running many copies as a repeatable "pay HP for mana" engine, especially paired with Rum (1 mana, heal 5) to top HP back off — this is the closest thing to a degenerate loop in the roster and isn't capped the way the design clearly intended other powerful effects to be.
- **The Kraken** (5 mana, 4 HP, 33% of current coins, 20 unblockable dmg, storage 12, capped at 1 copy): correctly the only capped-at-1 card and appropriately taxed, but Captain Nurgle's `_weightKraken = 6` (far above every other weight in that table, next-highest is `_weightActionHeal = 2.2`) makes Nurgle spam it almost every time it's playable, per `EnemyAI.PickCard`'s weighted-random pool — this reads as a one-note "big number" opponent rather than a varied one.
- **Siren Song** (3 mana, next attack unblockable) is a flat, uncapped answer to both reactions (Dead Man's Turn negates 100%, Counter Gale reflects 50% per `CombatResolver.ResolveCounterGale`'s `Mathf.FloorToInt(dmg*0.5f)`). Full negation of a charged reaction for 3 mana plus the cost of the attack itself is a big tempo/mana ask early (starting mana is 3, `StartingMaxMana`), but trivial once High Spirits/Treasure Chest/mana upgrades push totals to 5-6+.
- **Locker's Return** (3 mana, retrieve 3 random cards from discard into deck) is the *only* mechanism that refills the no-reshuffle deck, making it a load-bearing card for any attrition-oriented deck, not just a nice-to-have.

### (B) Systemic/economy issues

- **MaxHandSize = 4** is tight relative to the deck-building freedom (`MaxCopiesInDeck = 99` on most cards, `BaseStorageCapacity = 80`). Combined with the no-reshuffle deck (confirmed prior finding, not re-litigated), a hand-clogging draw like Treasure Chest's guaranteed +2 cards (`ignoreHandLimit: true`, pushing toward `BonusMaxHandSize = 6`) can leave a player sitting at 5-6 cards deep into a long game with no further draws once the 20-90 slot deck is exhausted — the deck-runs-dry disadvantage is real and asymmetric (whichever side draws through its deck first structurally loses card access first).
- **Essence Plunder's uncapped copy count** (see A) is the standout economy risk: it's the only 0-mana, no-condition mana-generation card, and nothing in `CardSO.MaxCopiesInDeck` restrains stacking it.
- **Reaction charges are genuinely invisible resources** per the existing known-mechanics list, but worth flagging for UX: `DeadMansTurn`/`CounterGale` have `_storageCost` of 8 and 7 respectively (the highest storage costs of any non-Kraken card) yet occupy a hand slot as an unplayable, silently-auto-converted "charge" — a new player has no way to intuit from the card in isolation that drawing it removes hand flexibility without a corresponding playable action.
- **Mana growth is entirely additive/permanent, never per-turn**: `GameConfigSO.StartingMaxMana = 3` (captains override to 4/5), and the only ways to raise it further are High Spirits (+1 permanent, 3 mana card) and Treasure Chest's 50% coin-flip +1. There's no scaling "turn number → bonus mana" curve, so games can stall at low mana ceilings if a player doesn't draw High Spirits/Treasure Chest.

### (C) AI &amp; difficulty curve issues

- `EnemyAI.ChooseReaction` computes fire probability as `weight / 2` with no clamp — Loreley's `_weightActionDefense = 1.8` yields a 90% Dead Man's Turn proc rate whenever charged, which will read to players as "the AI always blocks," not a personality trait.
- Captain weight tables are wildly divergent in scale (Nurgle's `_weightKraken = 6` vs. everything else in the 0.3-2.2 range), so `WeightedRandom` will overwhelmingly select Kraken whenever legal for Nurgle — a de facto scripted play rather than a weighted choice.
- `EnemyThinkTimeMin`/`Max` are both hardcoded to `1` in `GameConfigSO.asset` (code defaults were 0.8/2.2), so the enemy currently has zero pacing variance — a minor but real polish regression from what the code intends.
- `ApplyReactionAwareness` only dampens/boosts *this turn's* candidate weights and only reacts to `playerHasDeadMansTurn`/`playerHasCounterGale` as booleans (not stack count or card value) — the AI can't distinguish "player has one charge left" from "player has two," so its caution level doesn't scale with actual threat.
- Rumboat's `_weightReactionCounter = 0` and `_weightPlayAroundReactions = 0` combined with Rumboat's deck (no Dead Man's Turn/Counter Gale entries in `CaptainRumboatDeckSO.asset`) makes Rumboat a pure glass-cannon with zero defensive tech — consistent with "Aggressive" flavor, but means Rumboat has no comeback mechanic if its opening burst fails.

### (D) Level/progression design issues

- `ProgressionSO.asset` tracks exactly three booleans (`_level1Beaten`, `_level2Beaten`, `_level3Beaten`) — the entire campaign is 3 fixed captain fights (Loreley 50 HP/4 mana, Nurgle 60 HP/5 mana, Rumboat 40 HP/4 mana) with no difficulty tiers, repeatable content, or scaling beyond those three decks.
- Reward variance is thin: `LevelReward_Loreley` gives 40/25/10 coins by HP-remaining band plus 2 unlock cards; `LevelReward_Nurgle` 50/35/15; `LevelReward_Rumboat` 30/20/10 — Rumboat, despite being fought (per deck construction) as an aggressive/harder-feeling matchup, actually pays the least, an inverted risk/reward curve if fight order is Rumboat→Loreley→Nurgle or similar.
- `UpgradeSO` costs are identical across all three stats (25/45/70 coins per level, 140 total, 420 to max all three) for very different power gains: Mana gives +1/+1/+1 (a huge, curve-defining resource), HP gives +5/+8/+12, Storage gives +20/+30/+40 (deck-size headroom, marginal in a 3-fight campcampaign). Flat pricing for such different power levels means Mana upgrades are the clear best buy at every tier.

### (E) Top 5 concrete recommendations

1. **Cap Essence Plunder's `MaxCopiesInDeck`** (e.g., to 2-3, matching the reactions) — it's currently the only free, uncapped mana-generation card and the single biggest degenerate-combo risk found.
2. **Buff or redesign Hail Storm and Whirlpool** — either raise total DOT damage above their flat-damage equivalents (Whale Ram/Lightning) to compensate for being slower and interruptible, or add a secondary effect (e.g., reduced enemy healing, stacking) to justify the tempo cost.
3. **Clamp `ChooseReaction`'s fire probability** and/or rescale `_weightActionDefense`/`_weightReactionCounter` so no captain exceeds ~70-80% proc rate — Loreley's 90% auto-block reads as unfair/scripted rather than as a personality.
4. **Rebalance `_weightKraken` for Nurgle** (6.0 vs. a 0.3-2.2 range everywhere else) down to roughly 2-3 so Nurgle's aggression reads as varied bursts rather than "always Kraken when legal."
5. **Differentiate `UpgradeSO.CoinCostPerLevel` per stat** — Mana's flat power (+1 max mana ≈ a full extra card's worth of resource per turn) currently costs the same as Storage's marginal deck-size bump; pricing Mana noticeably higher (or Storage/HP lower) would make the upgrade shop a real strategic choice instead of a "always buy Mana first" default.</result>
