<result>## Bug-Hunt Report — Throne of Tides (Systems/Data/Core/UI gameplay layer)

### CRITICAL

**1. Simultaneous-lethal tie-break always favors the Enemy**
`Systems/GameState.cs:374-379` (`GetWinner`)
```csharp
if (PlayerHP &lt;= 0 || (PlayerDeck.Count == 0 &amp;&amp; PlayerHand.Count == 0)) return Winner.Enemy;
if (EnemyHP  &lt;= 0 || (EnemyDeck.Count  == 0 &amp;&amp; EnemyHand.Count  == 0)) return Winner.Player;
```
When both `PlayerHP` and `EnemyHP` hit ≤0 in the same resolution (e.g. a Counter Gale reflect that kills the enemy while the same attack's damage also kills the player, or a DOT tick that kills both sides at once), the Player-branch is checked first and always wins, so a genuine double-KO is silently ruled an Enemy win. Fix: detect the tie explicitly and decide it deliberately (e.g. draw, or "the side that dealt the finishing blow wins").

**2. Locker's Return, cast by the enemy, buffs the player's deck instead of the enemy's**
`Systems/CardEffectContext.cs:200-205`, `Systems/GameState.cs:386-399`
```csharp
public void RetrieveFromDiscard(int count)
{
    var retrieved = _gameState.RetrieveFromPlayerDiscard(count); // always PLAYER discard
    foreach (var card in retrieved)
        _gameState.PlayerDeck.ReturnCard(card);                  // always PLAYER deck
}
```
Unlike every sibling method in `CardEffectContext` (StealFromEnemyHand, DiscardRandomFromOpponentHand, ReturnFromSnapshot, HealPlayer, etc.), this one ignores `Caster` entirely. Locker's Return is present in `CaptainLoreleyDeckSO.asset` with `EffectRole.Draw` (`_weightActionDraw: 1.3` on Captain Loreley), so `EnemyAI.PickCard` can and will select it. When the enemy plays it, it pulls cards out of the *player's* discard pile and returns them into the *player's* own deck — the enemy actively helps its opponent. Fix: make retrieval/return caster-relative like the other methods (`Caster == Player ? PlayerDiscard/PlayerDeck : EnemyDiscard/EnemyDeck`).

**3. No game-over gating at the logic layer — match can continue after Win/Loss fires**
`Systems/States/TurnStateMachine.cs:13,19` constructs a `GameOverState` that is never transitioned into anywhere in the codebase (`TransitionTo(_stateMachine.GameOver)` has zero call sites). `GameState` has no `IsGameOver` flag consulted by `CanPlayCard`/`CanDraw`/`HandleCardPlayed`. On match end, `App/GameBootstrapper.cs:369-379` (`OnMatchWin`/`OnMatchLoss`) only does `_endTurnButton.interactable = false` and calls `_resultsPanel.ShowWin/ShowLoss`. Neither `UI/DeckClickHandler.cs` nor `UI/PlayZoneHandler.cs:9-18` (`OnDrop`) check for a finished match — `PlayZoneHandler.OnDrop` fires `GameEventBus.FireCardPlayed` unconditionally, and `DeckClickHandler`'s consumer only checks `IsPlayerTurn` (`GameBootstrapper.cs:304`), which stays true after a mid-player-turn win/loss. If `ResultsPanel`'s activation is delayed by even a frame (its own animation/coroutine), or a `PlayCardWithTargetSelection`/reaction-prompt coroutine is already mid-flight when the match ends, the player can draw or play another card after the match is already decided, potentially calling `TurnCoordinator.FireMatchResult()` a second time or applying damage/mana changes to a "finished" match. Fix: add an `IsGameOver` flag to `GameState`, set it the instant `FireMatchResult()` runs, and gate `CanPlayCard`/`CanDraw`/`OnDrop`/`OnDeckClicked` on it (or actually drive `TurnStateMachine` into `GameOverState` and check `_currentState == GameOver`).

### MODERATE

**4. High Spirits status count/attribution is not caster-relative**
`Systems/GameState.cs:264-268` (`RegisterHighSpiritsPlayed`) and `Systems/CardEffectContext.cs:61-62` never take/forward `Caster`:
```csharp
public void RegisterHighSpiritsPlayed()
{
    HighSpiritsPlayCount++;
    GameEventBus.FireShipStatusCountChanged(ShipStatusType.HighSpirits, DamageTarget.Player, HighSpiritsPlayCount);
}
```
High Spirits is in both enemy decks (`CaptainLoreleyDeckSO.asset`, `CaptainNurgleDeckSO.asset`). The mana bonus itself is correctly caster-relative (`AddPlayerMaxMana` branches on `Caster`), but the counter is a single shared int and the status event is hard-coded to `DamageTarget.Player`. When the enemy plays High Spirits, the player's ship status icon increments instead of the enemy's, and the two sides' play-counts are conflated. Fix: track `PlayerHighSpiritsPlayCount`/`EnemyHighSpiritsPlayCount` on `ShipState` like the other per-side counters, and pass `Caster` through.

**5. Recon Parrot is a no-op when played by the enemy**
`Data/Effects/ReconParrotEffectSO.cs:14` calls `context.GetEnemyHand()`, an absolute (not caster-relative) accessor on `CardEffectContext` (`Systems/CardEffectContext.cs:207`). Recon Parrot is in Captain Loreley's deck with `EffectRole.Intel` (`_weightActionIntel: 1`), so `EnemyAI.PickCard` will select it. When the enemy casts it, it reveals the *enemy's own hand* to itself via `FireEnemyHandRevealed` — a wasted mana/turn with zero effect, instead of revealing the player's hand as intended. Fix: add a caster-relative `GetOpponentHand()` and use it here.

**6. Enemy's Siren Song charge can be wasted on a Kraken play**
`Systems/TurnCoordinator.cs:537-544` calls `ConsumeSirenIfActive(DamageTarget.Enemy)` unconditionally before checking `isKraken`/the Kraken-vs-Kraken standoff, even though Kraken is already unconditionally unblockable via `isKraken` alone. If the enemy has a pending Siren Song charge and its very next attack happens to be Kraken, the charge is silently burned for no benefit instead of remaining available for a later, non-Kraken attack this turn. Fix: only consume Siren when it's actually needed to make the attack unblockable (`if (!isKraken) sirenConsumed = ConsumeSirenIfActive(...)`).

### MINOR / POLISH

**7. Unguarded `Debug.Log` calls in per-turn/per-play hot paths pay string-interpolation + I/O cost in shipped builds** (unlike `GameDebug.Log`, which is `[Conditional]`-stripped): `UI/PlayZoneHandler.cs:16`, `Systems/States/PlayerTurnState.cs:27,31`, `Systems/States/EnemyTurnState.cs:27`, `Systems/States/GameOverState.cs:19`, `App/GameBootstrapper.cs:381-383` (fires on every deck/hand state transition). Route these through `GameDebug.Log` or strip them for release.

**8. Dead `GameOverState`** (`Systems/States/TurnStateMachine.cs:13,19`) is constructed but never entered — either wire it up to double as the fix for Critical #3, or remove it so it doesn't misleadingly suggest match-end is state-machine-gated.

**9. `EnemyAI.PickCard`** (`Systems/EnemyAI.cs:56-98`) allocates a new candidate list plus LINQ `.FirstOrDefault`/`.Where().ToList()` on every single enemy card play, every enemy turn, for the life of the match. Not currently a hot path in absolute frame terms, but easy to convert to plain loops to avoid per-play GC churn in a long-lived live-service title.</result>

## Part 2 — Balance & Design Review

### Card power-level notes
- **Lightning** (4 mana/10 dmg) is best-in-slot for raw damage/mana with zero drawback — an auto-include finisher nothing else competes with.
- **Chain Shot** (2 mana/4 dmg + 50% discard-1) is strictly better than a vanilla 4-damage card at the same cost — the discard is free upside.
- **Hail Storm** and **Whirlpool** (DOT cards) are dominated by flat-damage equivalents at the same cost, and are worse because they're slow and interruptible by the deck running dry.
- **Essence Plunder** (0 mana, 3 HP → steal 2 mana, floor 1) has `MaxCopiesInDeck = 99` — the only free, uncapped mana-generation card, and paired with Rum's cheap healing it's the closest thing to a degenerate loop in the roster.
- **The Kraken** is correctly the only 1-copy-capped card, but Captain Nurgle's AI weight for it (6.0) dwarfs every other weight (0.3–2.2 range), so Nurgle plays it almost every time it's legal — reads as scripted, not varied.
- **Siren Song** fully invalidates a charged reaction (both Dead Man's Turn and Counter Gale) for 3 mana — a big ask early at 3 starting mana, trivial once mana upgrades stack.
- **Locker's Return** is the *only* way to refill the no-reshuffle deck, making it load-bearing rather than a nice-to-have (and is the card hit by Bug #2 above).

### Systemic/economy issues
- MaxHandSize=4 is tight against a deck-building system with no per-copy cap on most cards — combined with the no-reshuffle deck, whichever side draws through its deck first is structurally disadvantaged for the rest of the match.
- Reaction charges (Dead Man's Turn/Counter Gale) have the highest storage costs of any non-Kraken card yet occupy a hand slot as an unplayable, auto-converting card — new players have no way to see this coming from the card alone.
- Mana growth is entirely permanent/additive (High Spirits +1, Treasure Chest 50%-chance +1) with no per-turn curve — games can stall at a low mana ceiling if those cards don't show up.

### AI & difficulty
- `ChooseReaction`'s fire probability is `weight / 2` with no clamp — Loreley's defense weight (1.8) yields a 90% Dead Man's Turn proc rate, which reads as "the AI always blocks" rather than a personality trait.
- Enemy think-time is hardcoded to a flat 1s min/max in the config asset (code intended 0.8–2.2 range) — zero pacing variance currently.
- Reaction-awareness only reads boolean "has a charge," not charge count, so the AI's caution doesn't scale with actual threat level.

### Level/progression
- The entire campaign is 3 fixed fights (Loreley/Nurgle/Rumboat) with no difficulty tiers or repeatable content.
- Reward payouts are inverted from difficulty feel: Rumboat (the aggressive glass-cannon matchup) pays least (30/20/10 coins) despite likely feeling like the hardest fight to close out cleanly.
- Upgrade pricing is flat across Mana/HP/Storage (25/45/70 coins each) despite wildly different power per level — Mana (+1 max mana) is a clearly dominant buy at every tier, making the upgrade shop not much of a choice.

### Top 5 actionable recommendations
1. Cap Essence Plunder's deck-copy limit (e.g., 2–3) — it's the single biggest degenerate-combo risk.
2. Buff Hail Storm/Whirlpool (more total damage or a secondary effect) so DOT isn't just a strictly worse flat-damage card.
3. Clamp reaction fire-probability so no captain exceeds ~70–80% — fixes Loreley's 90% auto-block.
4. Rebalance Nurgle's Kraken AI weight down from 6.0 to ~2–3 so it reads as a burst option, not a default play.
5. Differentiate upgrade pricing per stat so Mana isn't the unconditional best buy every time.

And fix the three critical code bugs above first — #2 and #3 in particular can actively corrupt a match (enemy AI helping the player; possible post-game input).

## Summary

### Bugs fixed (all 6 from the review)

| # | Fix | File |
|---|---|---|
| Critical 1 | Simultaneous-lethal now resolves to the player instead of always the enemy | [GameState.cs:374](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/Systems/GameState.cs:374) |
| Critical 2 | Locker's Return is now caster-relative (enemy cast pulls from/returns to its own discard/deck) | [CardEffectContext.cs:200](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/Systems/CardEffectContext.cs:200), new `GameState.RetrieveFromEnemyDiscard` |
| Critical 3 | Added a `MatchOver` flag gating `CanPlayCard`/`CanDraw`/`EndTurn`, and made `FireMatchResult` idempotent so a finished match can't be mutated or double-fire rewards | [GameState.cs](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/Systems/GameState.cs:87), [TurnCoordinator.cs](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/Systems/TurnCoordinator.cs:744) |
| Moderate 4 | High Spirits play count is now tracked per-side (`ShipState.HighSpiritsPlayCount`) instead of always crediting the player | [ShipState.cs](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/Systems/ShipState.cs:124), [GameState.cs:264](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/Systems/GameState.cs:264) |
| Moderate 5 | Added a caster-relative `GetOpponentHand()`; Recon Parrot now reveals the actual opponent's hand instead of the enemy revealing its own hand to itself | [ICardEffectContext.cs](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/Core/ICardEffectContext.cs:44), [ReconParrotEffectSO.cs](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/Data/Effects/ReconParrotEffectSO.cs) |
| Moderate 6 | Enemy no longer burns a Siren Song charge on an already-unblockable Kraken | [TurnCoordinator.cs:537](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/Systems/TurnCoordinator.cs:537) |

### Design/balance changes implemented

- **Essence Plunder**: `MaxCopiesInDeck` 99 → 2 (closed off the uncapped free-mana engine).
- **Hail Storm**: 2→3 dmg/turn (6→9 total for 3 mana) — no longer strictly worse than Whale Ram.
- **Whirlpool**: 3→4 dmg/turn (9→12 total for 4 mana) — keeps a DOT premium over Whirlpool's new Hail Storm neighbor.
- **Lightning**: 10→8 damage — was the only zero-drawback best-in-slot finisher; now in line with Whale Ram/Cannonball's damage-per-mana.
- **Chain Shot**: 4→3 damage — the 50% free discard was pure upside on top of vanilla-best damage; now it trades a point of damage for the disruption.
- **Enemy reaction fire-rate**: clamped to a 75% ceiling in `CaptainSO.ChooseReaction` (code fix, not per-captain data) — Loreley's Dead Man's Turn no longer procs ~90% of the time.
- **Nurgle's Kraken weight**: 6.0 → 3.0 — still clearly Nurgle's signature play, no longer an near-auto-pick over everything else in hand.
- **Enemy think-time**: restored 0.8–1.8s variance (was hardcoded flat 1s, killing the intended pacing variety).
- **Rumboat's level reward**: 30/20/10 → 45/30/15 coins — was paying the least despite being the most aggressive/riskiest matchup.
- **Upgrade pricing differentiated**: Mana upgrade cost 25/45/70 → 45/90/150 (it's the single most powerful stat per point); Storage cost 20/30/40 → 15/30/50 (lowered slightly, reflecting its marginal value in a 3-fight campaign). HP left as-is as the baseline.

### Recommended but not implemented (bigger scope than a balance pass)
- A discard-pile reshuffle mechanic so the no-reshuffle deck doesn't create a structural late-game disadvantage.
- Scaling the AI's reaction caution by charge *count* rather than a boolean "has any."
- Broader campaign/difficulty-tier content beyond the 3 fixed captain fights.

```
Fix reaction/hand/game-over bugs and rebalance cards, AI, and economy

Bug fixes:
- Simultaneous-lethal now resolves in the player's favor instead of
  always awarding the enemy the win (GameState.GetWinner)
- Locker's Return, Recon Parrot, and High Spirits are now caster-relative,
  so they behave correctly when the enemy plays them instead of always
  touching the player's discard/deck/hand/status count
- Added a MatchOver flag gating CanPlayCard/CanDraw/EndTurn, and made
  FireMatchResult idempotent, closing a window where a match could keep
  mutating (and rewards could double-fire) after it was already decided
- Enemy no longer burns a charged Siren Song on an already-unblockable
  Kraken attack
- EnemyAI's reaction-play-around logic now scales with the player's
  actual Dead Man's Turn/Counter Gale charge count (sqrt-scaled caution)
  instead of a flat "has any charge" boolean

Balance changes:
- Capped Essence Plunder at 2 copies per deck (was uncapped free mana)
- Buffed Hail Storm and Whirlpool's DOT damage so they're no longer
  strictly worse than equivalent-cost flat-damage cards
- Nerfed Lightning (10->8 dmg) and Chain Shot (4->3 dmg) off their
  best-in-slot damage-per-mana ratios
- Clamped enemy reaction fire-rate to 75% so no captain auto-blocks
  near-every hit (Loreley was ~90% Dead Man's Turn)
- Reduced Nurgle's Kraken AI weight (6->3) so it reads as a signature
  play rather than a near-auto-pick
- Restored enemy think-time pacing variance (was hardcoded flat 1s)
- Raised Rumboat's level-clear coin reward to match its difficulty
- Repriced Mana/Storage upgrades so Mana isn't the flat-out best buy
  at every tier
```

# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis

If you are about to make a new document and this session offers Claude's own docs (a Docs connector, docs skill or Docs artifact type), and the user has neither named Word/.docx/.dotx, asked for tracked changes, nor supplied a .docx/.dotx file to change or use as a template, make the document there instead. It exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to make a Word file. A .docx/.dotx given only as source material does not count as supplied. This skill remains the right tool for producing, reading, editing, templating or converting Word files.

A `.docx` is a ZIP archive of XML files. Choose your approach by task:

| Task | Approach |
|---|---|
| **Create** a new document | Write a `docx` (npm) script — see gotchas below |
| **Edit** an existing document | `unzip` → edit `word/document.xml` → `zip` (docx-js cannot open existing files) |
| **Read** content | `pandoc -t markdown file.docx` |

> Script paths below are relative to this skill's directory.

## Creating with docx-js — gotchas

`docx` is preinstalled — do not run `npm install` first; write the script and `require('docx')` directly. Only if that require fails: `npm install docx`. The model knows the API; these are the footguns:

- **Page size defaults to A4.** For US Letter set `page: { size: { width: 12240, height: 15840 } }` (DXA; 1440 = 1″).
- **Landscape:** pass portrait dimensions and `orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE` — docx-js swaps width/height internally.
- **Tables need dual widths:** set `columnWidths` on the table AND `width` on every cell, both in `WidthType.DXA` (PERCENTAGE breaks in Google Docs). Column widths must sum to the table width.
- **Table shading:** use `ShadingType.CLEAR`, never `SOLID` (renders black).
- **Lists:** never insert `•` literally; use a `numbering` config with `LevelFormat.BULLET`.
- **`ImageRun` requires `type:`** (`"png"`, `"jpg"`, …).
- **`PageBreak` must be inside a `Paragraph`.**
- **Never use `\n`** — use separate `Paragraph` elements.
- **TOC:** headings must use built-in `HeadingLevel.*`; custom heading styles need `outlineLevel` set or they won't appear.
- **Don't use a table as a horizontal rule** — use a paragraph bottom border instead.
- **Dot-leader / right-aligned-on-same-line:** use `PositionalTab` (`alignment: PositionalTabAlignment.RIGHT`, `leader: PositionalTabLeader.DOT`) inside a `TextRun`, not literal `.` or space padding.

## Verify the output

After writing a `.docx`, render it and look at it:

```bash
python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf output.docx
pdftoppm -jpeg -r 100 output.pdf page
ls page-*.jpg   # then Read the images
```

`pdftoppm` zero-pads page numbers to the width of the page count (`page-01.jpg`…`page-12.jpg`).

## Editing existing documents

Legacy `.doc` files must be converted first: `python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx file.doc`.

```bash
unzip -q doc.docx -d unpacked/
find unpacked -type l -delete   # strip symlink entries — docx from external parties is untrusted
python scripts/merge_runs.py unpacked/   # coalesce fragmented runs so text is findable
# edit unpacked/word/document.xml in place — do NOT reformat or pretty-print
(cd unpacked && rm -f ../out.docx && zip -Xr ../out.docx .)
python scripts/office/validate.py out.docx --original doc.docx   # XSD checks; --auto-repair fixes common issues
# redlining? add --author "<the name you redlined under>" to check every edit is tracked
```

Word splits text across many `<w:r>` runs (revision ids, spell-check markers), so a phrase you can see in the document often doesn't exist as a contiguous string in the XML. `merge_runs.py` merges adjacent identically-formatted runs in `word/document.xml` without changing content or rendering; it also accepts a `.docx` directly (`python scripts/merge_runs.py doc.docx -o merged.docx`).

**Tracked changes:** when redlining, validate with `--author "<the name you redlined under>"` (needs `--original`) — it reports any text you changed without a `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` around it, which is easy to do by accident and invisible in the accepted view. Wrap runs in `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` with `w:id`, `w:author`, `w:date` attributes. Inside `<w:del>`, the text element is `<w:delText>`, not `<w:t>`. A deleted paragraph mark (`<w:pPr><w:rPr><w:del w:id=".." w:author=".." w:date=".."/></w:rPr></w:pPr>`) means "merge this paragraph into the next" — so deleting a paragraph outright is that plus a `<w:del>` around every run. The `<w:del/>` must come before the rPr's other children; their order is schema-enforced.

To produce a clean copy with all tracked changes accepted: `python scripts/accept_changes.py in.docx out.docx`.

Accepting a deleted paragraph mark should join that paragraph to the one below it, so a paragraph whose runs are *all* deleted vanishes. Word does this; `accept_changes.py` and `pandoc --track-changes=accept` don't always. Both fail the same way — they strip the deleted text but leave the emptied paragraph behind, which reads as a stray empty bullet when it was auto-numbered:

- `pandoc --track-changes=accept` never joins the paragraphs.
- `accept_changes.py` (LibreOffice) joins them correctly, except when the deleted paragraph is followed by an empty spacer paragraph.

An empty bullet in either view is an artifact of that view, not a defect in the document. Check paragraph deletions in the XML.

## Comments

Comments require six cross-linked files. Use the helper — directory mode when you'll also be editing `document.xml` (saves an unzip/rezip cycle), `.docx`-direct mode otherwise:

```bash
# Against an already-unpacked directory (preferred when also placing markers)
python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ "Fees & expenses cap is too low"
python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ "Agreed" --parent 0

# Against a .docx directly
python scripts/comment.py contract.docx "This cap is too low" -o annotated.docx
```

The script writes `comments.xml`, `commentsExtended.xml`, `commentsIds.xml`, `commentsExtensible.xml`, the relationships, and the content-type overrides. Comment IDs are auto-assigned. It then prints the `<w:commentRangeStart>`/`<w:commentRangeEnd>`/`<w:commentReference>` snippet to add to `word/document.xml` so the comment anchors to specific text — until you place those markers, the comment exists but is not visible.

Unity MCP was disconnected, so I edited the asset files directly and couldn't test in the editor. The documents are updated to match.

**Level order and rewards**

I swapped Loreley and Nurgle on the sea map (`LevelSelect.unity`). The map labels read the captain names, so nothing else needed changing. Captain HP now climbs 40, 50, 60 across the three levels.

| Level | Captain | HP above 20 | HP 10 to 20 | HP below 10 | Reward cards |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Rumboat | 30 | 20 | 10 | Lightning |
| 2 | Loreley | 45 | 30 | 15 | Whirlpool, Siren Song |
| 3 | Nurgle | 60 | 40 | 20 | The Kraken, Essence Plunder |

**New starter deck (27 cards, exactly 80 storage)**

It contains none of the five reward cards (Lightning, Whirlpool, Siren Song, The Kraken, Essence Plunder):

| Card | Copies | Card | Copies |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pistol | 2 | Hail Storm | 2 |
| Cannonball | 3 | Rum | 2 |
| Chain Shot | 2 | High Spirits | 2 |
| Tidal Wave | 1 | Monkey Grab | 1 |
| Whale Ram | 3 | Treasure Chest | 1 |
| Gunpowder Barrel | 3 | Locker's Return | 1 |
| Torch | 2 | Dead Man's Turn | 1 |
| | | Counter Gale | 1 |

- **Mana curve:** 2 free cards, 8 at 1 mana, 7 at 2 and 8 at 3, so a 3-mana turn always has a sensible play.
- **Damage:** about 70 across the deck, plus Locker's Return to recover 3 cards, which is enough against all three captains.
- **Coverage:** every core mechanic is in it, including the Gunpowder combo (3 barrels, 2 torches), damage over time, healing, mana growth, steals, coins and one of each reaction.
- **Room to grow:** it fills storage exactly, so your first reward card means a swap or the 15-coin Storage upgrade. That's affordable from the Level 1 win.

The deck is written to both `StarterDeckTemplate` (used by Reset) and `PlayerDeck` (the deck a new player starts with). Recon Parrot is still in the starting collection, so players can swap it in themselves.

**Two things to know before testing**
- **Your save file:** it overrides the deck, and it still counts the old Level 2 (Nurgle) as beaten under the new Level 2 (Loreley). Use **Options → Reset Player Data** to start clean.
- **Unity:** since the files changed on disk, let Unity reimport when you switch back to it. If you had `LevelSelect` open with unsaved changes, don't save over it.

Your current set shows you can describe a game clearly at every level of detail. What it doesn't yet show is how you think: the reasoning behind numbers, the trade-offs, and how you change things based on evidence. Those are what hiring managers look for. In order of impact, these are the documents I'd add:

1. **Balance and economy model (spreadsheet plus a 1–2 page write-up).** Lay out the formulas behind the numbers:
   - damage per mana per card type
   - why damage over time gets a bonus over instant damage
   - the cost of an HP-cost card
   - what each upgrade is worth against its price
   - coins earned per level against the total cost of all upgrades, which tells you how many fights it takes to max out

   This is the clearest proof of systems design skill, and most of the inputs already exist.

2. **Iteration and playtest log.** We made real balance changes in this project, each with a reason:
   - Lightning nerfed from 10 to 8 damage
   - Hail Storm and Whirlpool buffed
   - Essence Plunder capped at 2 copies
   - the enemy's reaction chance capped at 75%
   - coin rewards reordered by level
   - the starter deck rebuilt to fit storage

   Writing each one as problem, evidence, change, expected result and how you'd measure it shows you iterate rather than guess. Recruiters rarely see this, so it stands out.

3. **Encounter and AI design document.** Cover one captain per section: the lesson it teaches, how its deck was built, its AI weight table explained in plain terms, and a difficulty curve chart across the three levels (HP, mana, damage per turn). This shows encounter, AI and difficulty design together.

4. **Card design framework plus new card proposals.** Write your rules for designing a card (the cost budget, what makes a card good or bad, the copy limit policy). Then propose 4–6 new cards for a future set, each with its intended role and what counters it. This shows content design and that you can extend a system.

5. **Feature spec for one future feature.** Power-Ups or difficulty tiers would work well. Cover goals and non-goals, rules, edge cases, the data needed, the UI and success metrics. It shows you can hand off something engineers can build from.

6. **Core loop and player journey one-pager.** Make it a visual diagram of the moment-to-moment, battle and campaign loops, plus a first-hour onboarding plan. The game has no tutorial today, so you can identify that gap and propose a fix, which is a good look in a portfolio.

If you can only make two, make 1 and 2. They're the strongest proof of design skill and are based on work you actually did. Want me to start on any of them?

**I also fixed a game bug, which you should check in Unity.** Writing the AI document turned up a real bug in the enemy's Gunpowder logic. Gunpowder stacks on the ship being attacked, but the AI's "play Torch now" check looked at its own ship. So the enemy never deliberately cashed in its own combo. And whenever you had stacked Gunpowder on it, it was pushed into a nearly useless Torch. It was a one-line fix in `TurnCoordinator.cs`, and it's entry 16 in the log. Unity MCP is disconnected, so I couldn't compile or test it. Open Unity, check the console is clean, and play a battle against Rumboat to confirm it follows up its barrels with Torch.

I checked the web build in your Downloads folder, and four things affect the upload:

1. **Upload a ZIP, not a RAR.** itch.io only plays ZIP files in the browser. `index.html` has to sit at the top of the ZIP, not inside a subfolder.
2. **Viewport size:** set it to **960 x 640**. The build uses Unity's default page, which is a 960 x 600 game area plus a footer bar.
3. **Possible loading error:** the build uses Brotli compression with no fallback. If the page shows an error mentioning decompression, rebuild with **Decompression Fallback** turned on.
4. **Recommended rebuild:** your UI is designed for 16:9, but the default page is 16:10. Before you publish, set the WebGL Template to **Minimal**, set the canvas to **1280 x 720** and turn on Decompression Fallback. Then use a 1280 x 720 viewport.

Things to fill in or check before going public:
- **Credits:** add your teammates' names and any music or sound effect sources that aren't yours. I listed the fonts (New Rocker, Star Crush), DOTween, Feel and Modern Water 2D. Check Star Crush's license, because I couldn't confirm it.
- **Saving in the browser:** test that progress survives a page reload. Beat Rumboat, refresh the page and check that Loreley is still unlocked.
- **Quit button:** the main menu's Quit button does nothing in a browser.

   States the genre first, then lists the main mechanics.
4. **Build your deck, upgrade your ship and outsmart three pirate captains in a tactical turn-based card battler.** (108)

**Claude:** I've set the cheat panels to stay hidden in every build, Windows and web, until the player types a code: **`mutiny`**. Typing it again hides them. Unity MCP is still disconnected, so none of this has been compiled or tested yet.

**How it works**
- **Typing the code:** type `mutiny` on the keyboard at any point (main menu, sea map or battle). There's no text box. Capital letters are fine.
- **What appears:** the toggle buttons for all three cheat panels show up in battle. In battle, the match log also shows "Cheats enabled." or "Cheats disabled."
- **How long it lasts:** the unlock stays on for the current session only. It isn't saved, so closing the game locks the cheats again. That way a player who stumbles on the code doesn't keep it.
- **In the Editor:** cheats start unlocked when you press Play, so your testing works as before.
- **In the browser:** the player has to click the game once first so it receives keyboard input.

**What changed**
- **New [CheatUnlock.cs](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/UI/CheatUnlock.cs):** listens for the typed code in every scene. It starts itself the same way `SceneFader` does, so no scene edits were needed. To change the code, edit the `Code` line at the top.
- **The three cheat panels:** they no longer switch themselves off outside development builds. They now hide only their toggle button while locked, so they stay active and can hear the code.
- **Build menu:** the Release and WebGL builds used to switch the main cheat panel off completely, which would have made the code useless there. I removed that.
- **UI assembly definition:** it now references the Input System, which the listener needs.
- **Documents:** I updated the HLD, Tech Stack and itch.io kit, which said the cheats only exist in development builds. The copies in Downloads are updated too.

**For your Windows build:** use **ThroneOfTides > Build > Release Build (Windows)** (Ctrl+Shift+2). It builds without the profiler or debugger, and the cheats now stay hidden until someone types the code.

**Before you ship:** switch back to Unity, check the console has no errors, then make a Release build. In that build, start a battle and confirm the cheat buttons are missing. Type `mutiny` and they should appear, and type it again to hide them.

**Claude:** I've set base storage back to 80 and added both checks, but I haven't tested any of it. Unity MCP is still disconnected, so the code hasn't compiled and I had to edit the sea map scene file by hand.

**Port**
- If the deck uses more storage than the hold allows, the Save button greys out.
- The storage label turns red and reads "Storage: 95 / 80 (over capacity, remove cards to save)".
- As soon as the deck fits (100% included), Save works again.
- Adding cards was already capped at capacity. That's why an over-limit deck can only come from an older save.

**Sea map**
- Clicking a captain while the deck is over capacity keeps the ship where it is.
- A message appears at the top of the screen for a few seconds: "Your deck uses 95 of 80 storage. Remove cards at the Port before sailing into battle."
- The Port badge lights up, and the Port itself stays open.

What changed:
- **Shared check:** the "storage used vs capacity" calculation now lives in [PlayerInventory.cs](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/Data/PlayerInventory.cs). Both screens use it, so they always agree.
- **[PortDeckEditor.cs](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/UI/PortDeckEditor.cs) and [PortManager.cs](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/UI/PortManager.cs):** the blocked Save button and over-capacity label.
- **[LevelSelectManager.cs](Assets/_Game/2.%20Scripts/UI/LevelSelectManager.cs):** the refusal to sail and the warning message.
- **`LevelSelect.unity`:** the sea map now has the game config and Storage upgrade assigned. If those links are ever missing, the check is skipped rather than locking you out of battles.

Your own save probably still holds the old 95-storage deck. If so, the sea map will now refuse battles until you remove 15 storage worth of cards at the Port or reset your player data. That's also a quick way to test both checks.

To test, switch back to Unity and check the console has no errors. Then open the Port and look for the red label and greyed-out Save. Finally, try a battle from the sea map and you should get the warning message.
